p01.why: On -m32 pointers, function pointers, and the type of nullptr have size 4; no main.

p02.why: short with double is a forbidden combination.

p03.why: Each sum is rounded to its type by the cast, and ties go to even, so every assertion holds even with GCC's extra precision on -m32.

p04.why: Specifier order does not matter and int adds nothing, so each pair names one type.

p05.why: A sign with bool is forbidden.

p06.why: long long with double is forbidden.

p07.why: The literals are the largest finite values of the three formats on x86-64, so every comparison holds.

p08.why: x87 long double has 64 bits of precision, so 2^53+1 is exact and 2^64+1 is a tie that rounds to even 2^64.

p09.why: float has 24 and double 53 bits of precision; 2^24+1 and 2^53+1 are ties that round to even, the smaller sums are exact.

p10.why: long double on -m32 is still 80-bit x87 with 64 bits of precision, so 2^53+1 is exact.

p12.why: A size with char is forbidden.

p13.why: The common type is the floating-point type of higher rank, and an integer operand of any rank gives the floating-point type.

p14.why: Round to nearest, ties to even, on x86-64 where double and float arithmetic is exact to the type.

p16.why: char is signed, so char(-1) is negative and char(200) keeps the low 8 bits as -56.

p18.why: A sign with wchar_t is forbidden; Clang's error is warning-controlled but on by default.

p19.why: On -m32 the type of sizeof and alignof is unsigned int.

p20.why: Unsigned wrap gives 2^N-1 at 32 and 64 bits, -int_max-1 does not overflow, and -1 to unsigned short is 65535.

p21.why: On -m32 unsigned long has 32 bits, so 0ul-1ul is 4294967295.

p22.why: On x86-64 the three sizes are 8.

p23.why: GCC and Clang give long long alignment 4 on -m32 and accept; EDG ILP32 gives 8 and rejects the second assertion.

p24.why: Each character type is distinct from char's sign variants and from its underlying type.

p25.why: On -m32 long and int have the same size but stay distinct types.

p26.why: On x86-64 each alignment equals the size, long double 16.

p27.why: Nonzero converts to true, and true+true is 2.

p28.why: A sign with float is forbidden.

p29.why: On x86-64 the type of sizeof and alignof is unsigned long.

p30.why: char then long long is 12 bytes with GCC and Clang on -m32 but 16 with EDG ILP32, so EDG rejects; char then double is 12 everywhere.

p31.why: bool, char8_t, char16_t, wchar_t and unsigned short promote to int; char32_t's values do not fit int, so it promotes to unsigned int.

p32.why: The formats are the same on -m32, so the largest values are the same.

p33.why: wchar_t is signed with underlying type int, so wchar_t(-1) is negative.

p34.why: A non-null address and 0.5 convert to true, 0.0 to false, false-true is -1, and nullptr may convert to bool in direct initialization.

p35.why: On -m32 long is 4 bytes and long long 8.

p36.why: int_max+1 overflows int, which is undefined, so the constexpr initializer is not a constant.

p38.why: long double may be written in either order; no main.

p39.why: A sign with char8_t is forbidden.

p40.why: char8_t has the values of unsigned char, so 256 wraps to 0 and -1 to 255; char32_t(-1) is 0xffffffff.

p41.why: A size with char is forbidden.

p42.why: On x86-64 long and long long are both 8 bytes but distinct types.

p44.why: The sizes are the same on -m32.

p45.why: On x86-64 each sum is rounded to its type at run time, ties to even, so no early return fires.

p46.why: char8_t, char16_t, char32_t are unsigned, so -1 gives their maximum, which is positive after promotion.

p47.why: On -m32 long and unsigned int share a size so 1L+1u is unsigned long; long long holds every unsigned long so 1LL+1ul is long long.

p48.why: The floating-point operand decides the type, and the higher floating-point rank wins.

p50.why: A size with float is forbidden.

p51.why: A sign with char32_t is forbidden.

p52.why: On -m32 long double has alignment 4, so char then long double takes 16 bytes with alignment 4.

p53.why: A size with bool is forbidden.

p56.why: A sign with char16_t is forbidden.

p57.why: A size with float is forbidden.

p59.why: On x86-64 long holds every unsigned int so 1L+1u is long; long long cannot hold every unsigned long, so 1LL+1ul is unsigned long long.
